question: When the sun, the moon and the earth are in a straight line, the height of the tide will be higher. What are these tides called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Spring tides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Spring tides occur when the sun, the moon, and the earth are in a straight line during the new moon and full moon phases.
 
• These tides are characterized by higher high tides and lower low tides due to the combined gravitational pull of the sun and the moon.
 
• The term "spring" does not refer to the season but rather the concept of "springing forth" in terms of increased tidal range.
 
• Spring tides happen approximately twice a month, during the full moon and new moon phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neap tides:**

 
 
• Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other (first and third quarters of the moon).
 
• These tides are characterized by a smaller tidal range, with lower high tides and higher low tides.
 
• The gravitational forces of the sun and the moon partially cancel each other out during neap tides.
 
 
 
• **Diurnal tide:**
 
 
• Diurnal tides refer to a tidal pattern with one high tide and one low tide each day.
 
• This type of tide is less common and typically occurs in certain geographical regions.
 
• Diurnal tides are found in areas such as the Gulf of Mexico and parts of Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational forces:**
 
 
• The gravitational pull of the moon and the sun affects the Earth's water, causing tides.
 
• The moon has a greater influence on tides due to its proximity to Earth compared to the sun.
 
• Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of gravitational forces exerted by the moon, the sun, and the rotation of the Earth.
